answer.evidence: The wooden post has a light tan top at rows 0-3, a darker edge line at row 4, and a brown front face at rows 5-13 with a dark base at row 14. That gives a top of about 4 rows over a front face of about 11 rows. The corrugated sheet band (left) and the checker sheet (right) are each drawn as a flat repeating pattern over rows 0-15, with no top-to-front transition and no edge line. They read as top-down or elevation strips rather than volumes, so not every major part shows a top. The main body is ambiguous between the post and the sheet band, and I measured the post.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin, tiny prop, so I judged it by eye and used the measured facts as support. It reads as a wooden post beside a band of overlapping grey corrugated sheet with light-to-dark steps, roughly 5 on the sheet band and fewer on the post. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans toward the adjacent material tone rather than a black sticker line. Near-flat coverage is 0%, with no 5x5 flat fills. It has 15 visible tones per tile, against 9 for the hedge, 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well, so it sits within the reference range for a single-tile prop. The corrugation and post grain give some texture, though it is less elaborate than the stall or well, which have per-piece highlights and clusters. A careful artist would accept it next to the references without it looking noticeably flatter.

answer.evidence: The post (x=5-7) has a tan top band in rows 0-3. Row 4 is a darker line, and an 11-row dark brown front face (rows 4-14) sits below it. That reads as a top plus a front face. The left corrugated sheet (x about 0-4) is a face-on vertical strip with repeating overlap bands and no top edge line, so it has no top surface. The checkered right strip is flat top-down texture with no front face. The post is the only part with a clear top plus front, so the object reads as three_quarter, but weakly.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin, narrow vertical strip: a dark wooden post beside a band of overlapping corrugated sheet tops. At this size I read about 4-5 lightness steps on the sheet band (highlight, light, mid, dark, deep) plus a separate shaded wood ramp for the post. The measured facts back this up: 15 visible tones per 16x16 tile, above prop-hedge (9) and close to prop-stall-cheese (17) and prop-well-roofed (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so no 5x5 area is a flat fill. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted. It leans brown or grey-brown beside the wood and metal rather than being a uniform black sticker line. Texture comes from the overlapping sheet ridges and the post grain, which is less lush than the stall or well but comparable to the hedge and bench. Nothing looks thinner or flatter than the references, so it would sit acceptably next to them. It is slightly shallower than the best references because the material ramps are compact.
